title: Prove: Idempotent consumers trade storage for safe retries
body:
Making message consumers idempotent allows at-least-once delivery and retries without duplicate side effects, at the cost of deduplication state, retention policy, and coordination.

Complexity: O(1) average deduplication check/record per message plus storage proportional to retained keys; enables correctness under at-least-once delivery.

title: Invariant: Idempotent consumers trade storage for safe retries
body: For a given idempotency key, applying the same operation more than once produces the same externally visible result as applying it once.

title: Proof step: Identify operations uniquely
body: Each message or request carries a stable idempotency key so repeated deliveries can be recognized as the same logical operation.

title: Proof step: Check-before-apply
body:
The consumer tests whether the key was already processed; constant-time hash lookups or set membership checks avoid linear scans as processed history grows.

Depends on: dedupe-key

title: Proof step: Record effect atomically enough
body:
On first application the consumer persists the result or marks the key seen so subsequent retries take the no-op/return-prior-result path.

Depends on: seen-check

title: Proof step: Safety gained, state and lifecycle added
body:
Retries become safe under redelivery and crashes, but the system must store, expire, and sometimes distribute dedupe state, and define behavior when keys collide or state is lost.

Depends on: record, seen-check
